title: Variae observationes circa series infinitas
version: original 1744 Latin publication scan with Euler Archive cover sheet
read_scope: Targeted reading of the primary text at Theorems 7–8, printed pp. 172–176.
main_result: Derives the multiplicative prime-product identity for reciprocal power sums and the divergence of the sum of reciprocals of primes.
classical_zeta_transfer_obstacle: The product is obtained in the region of convergence or via positive partial products. Its existence gives no zero exclusion inside the critical strip.

title: Beweis des Satzes, daß jede unbegrenzte arithmetische Progression, deren erstes Glied und Differenz ganze Zahlen ohne gemeinschaftlichen Factor sind, unendlich viele Primzahlen enthält
venue: Abhandlungen der Königlich Preussischen Akademie der Wissenschaften, 45–71
version: original journal reproduction hosted by Rutgers, with library cover
read_scope: Targeted reading of the primary text at pp. 45–46, and the conclusion on pp. 69–71.
source_locator: pp. 45–46, and the conclusion on pp. 69–71
main_result: Proves infinitude of primes in every reduced arithmetic progression by decomposing a progression into characters and establishing the required nonvanishing at the real point 1.
classical_zeta_transfer_obstacle: The nonvanishing argument is at a boundary point for Dirichlet series. It does not control nontrivial zeros of the ordinary zeta function.

title: Sur la totalité des nombres premiers inférieurs à une limite donnée
venue: Journal de Mathématiques Pures et Appliquées 17, 341–365
version: digitized original journal, proceedings or seminar publication
read_scope: Targeted reading of the primary text at opening statement and closing estimates.
main_result: Studies the prime counting function via factorials and the summatory logarithms of primes, and constrains possible asymptotics, including the constant of any existing prime-number-theorem ratio.
classical_zeta_transfer_obstacle: The arguments give constraints on prime counts and possible asymptotic expansions. They do not supply bounds on zeta zeros in the critical strip.

title: Mémoire sur les nombres premiers
venue: Journal de Mathématiques Pures et Appliquées 17, 366–390
version: digitized original journal, proceedings or seminar publication
read_scope: Targeted reading of the primary text at pp. 382–390, prime-count bounds and proof of Bertrand's postulate.
source_locator: pp. 382–390, prime-count bounds and proof of Bertrand's postulate
main_result: Gives explicit upper and lower comparisons for prime counts and proves the stated prime-existence interval of Bertrand.
classical_zeta_transfer_obstacle: Finite intervals and constant-factor bounds are compatible with error terms far larger than the square-root scale in RH.

title: Sur quelques problèmes relatifs à la distribution des nombres premiers
venue: Bulletin de la Société Mathématique de France 28, 25–38
version: digitized original journal, proceedings or seminar publication
read_scope: Targeted reading of the primary text at §1 and closing equations (13)–(14).
main_result: Uses partial summation to move between weighted prime-counting statements. In particular the theorem for the sum of log p directly yields the corresponding logarithmic integral estimate without a second contour argument.
classical_zeta_transfer_obstacle: Partial summation preserves the scale of an available PNT remainder. It does not create the square-root scale necessary to constrain critical-strip zeros.

title: Sur quelques inégalités dans la théorie de la fonction ζ(s) de Riemann
venue: Bulletin de la Société Mathématique de France 33, 229–241
version: digitized original journal, proceedings or seminar publication
read_scope: Targeted reading of the primary text at §§I and III, including (23)–(27).
main_result: Investigates inequalities for ζ near the edge of the critical strip and applies reciprocal-zeta estimates to sharpen the error for the squarefree counting function.
classical_zeta_transfer_obstacle: The reciprocal-zeta estimate applies on its specified boundary and contours. The resulting squarefree asymptotic does not establish a zero-free critical half-strip.
correction_history: Numdam metadata says intégrales, while the printed heading at p. 229 says inégalités. The title follows the printed article.

title: Sur une propriété fonctionnelle de la fonction ζ(s) de Riemann
venue: Bulletin de la Société Mathématique de France 37, 59–60
version: digitized original journal, proceedings or seminar publication
read_scope: Read both printed pages, including the Jensen antecedent, the two characterizing identities, their asymptotic normalization and the majorant argument.
main_result: Each of two shifted-argument identities, together with ζ(s+n) tending to 1, separately characterizes the zeta function. The iteration for (4) uses positive coefficients and majorizes the one for (3).
classical_zeta_transfer_obstacle: Positivity controls the recursion and its convergence. It is not the positivity of a spectral form over all zeros.

title: Le énième nombre premier comme valeur asymptotique d’une fonction déduite de la fonction ζ(s) de Riemann
venue: Bulletin de la Société Mathématique de France 53, 226–234
version: digitized original journal, proceedings or seminar publication
read_scope: Targeted reading of the primary text at §§1–2 and applications to p_n in the later sections.
source_locator: §§1–2 and applications to p_n in the later sections
main_result: Recovers successive exponents and coefficients of a Dirichlet series from its real-axis asymptotics, and applies the extraction to functions of ζ to recover a fixed nth prime.
classical_zeta_transfer_obstacle: The limit sends real s to infinity for a fixed prime index. It gives no uniform inversion near the critical strip and no bound on off-line zeros.

title: Sur l’ordre de grandeur de la fonction ζ(s) de Riemann dans la bande critique
venue: Annales de la Faculté des Sciences de Toulouse 22, 1–39
version: digitized original journal, proceedings or seminar publication

source_locator: Introduction and exponential-sum estimate applied to ζ in the last sections
main_result: Derives improvements for bounds on the size of ζ in the critical strip by estimating oscillatory sums arising from its analytic representation.
classical_zeta_transfer_obstacle: An upper bound on the modulus of ζ in a strip leaves open the location of its zeros there.

title: Geometrisches zur Riemannschen Zetafunktion
version: original Mathematische Annalen volume 110 scan with GDZ coversheet dated 1935
read_scope: Targeted reading of the primary text at pp. 517–519, discussion of level curves and branch points.
source_locator: pp. 517–519, discussion of level curves and branch points
main_result: Relates the Riemann hypothesis to the absence of nontrivial ζ′ zeros to the left of the critical line by studying the level curves of ζ.
classical_zeta_transfer_obstacle: This transfers the needed global zero exclusion to a derivative and supplies a geometric way to phrase it. The exclusion itself is still required.
correction_history: 1934 appears in some indexes and is the receipt year. This entry follows the 1935 volume year recorded on the GDZ wrapper.

title: Zeros of the derivatives of the Riemann zeta-function
version: digitized original journal, proceedings or seminar publication
read_scope: Targeted reading of the primary text at Theorem 1, equations (1.1)–(1.2), and its corollary.
main_result: The counts of ζ and ζ′ zeros in the left half of the critical strip up to height T differ by O(log T). The ensuing corollary gives an explicit derivative nonvanishing equivalent to RH.
classical_zeta_transfer_obstacle: The comparison relates two potentially nonempty collections of zeros, so a separate argument is needed to exclude every ζ′ zero in that region.

title: Asymptotic Formula for the Coordinates of the Zeros of Sections of the Zeta Function, ζ_N(s), Near s = 1
version: original PNAS printed page images assembled from PMC CDN into a PDF
read_scope: Targeted reading of the primary text at Abstract and §1, and the concluding location argument.
source_locator: Abstract and §1, and the concluding location argument
main_result: For finite Dirichlet sections ζ_N, estimates the zeros near 1 at large N and establishes the stated left-of-1 position in that range.
classical_zeta_transfer_obstacle: The zeros of truncations and those of meromorphic ζ are distinct. Uniform convergence of the finite Dirichlet sums is available strictly to the right of 1, outside the intended critical region.

title: Generalization of Recent Method Giving Lower Bound for N₀(T) of Riemann’s Zeta-Function
version: original PNAS printed page images assembled from PMC CDN into a PDF
read_scope: Targeted reading of the primary text at p. 3984, the polynomial condition and equation (1).
source_locator: p. 3984, the polynomial condition and equation (1)
main_result: Generalizes a lower-bound argument for critical-line zeros by replacing the linear polynomial in the approximate Dirichlet expression with P satisfying P(0)=0 and P(x)+P(1−x)=1.
classical_zeta_transfer_obstacle: The polynomial freedom affects bounds for the proportion of zeros on the line. It does not rule out individual exceptions.

title: Almost All Roots of ζ(s) = a Are Arbitrarily Close to σ = 1/2
version: original PNAS printed page images assembled from PMC CDN into a PDF
read_scope: Read all three printed pages, including the mean-square lemma, weighted root sums, the separate left and right tails, the a=1 modification and the closing note about Selberg's refinement.
source_locator: main Theorem, p. 1322, with Lemmas 1–6 and proof on pp. 1322–1323
main_result: For fixed complex a and T^(1/2)≤U≤T, all but O(U log T/log log T) roots of ζ(s)=a with T<t<T+U lie within (log log T)^2/log T of the critical line. The inner count has main term U log T/(2π).
classical_zeta_transfer_obstacle: The same clustering holds even for nonzero target values. A density-one asymptotic for a shrinking strip does not prove exact location of every zero.

title: Deduction of Semi-Optimal Mollifier for Obtaining Lower Bound for N₀(T) for Riemann’s Zeta-Function
version: original PNAS printed page images assembled from PMC CDN into a PDF
read_scope: Read all four printed pages, following the choice of dominant term, the boundary constraints H(0)=0 and H(log y)=1, the optimized profile, and the final comparison in (33).
main_result: Derives an Euler–Lagrange equation after smoothing an optimization of the dominant contribution in Levinson's mollified mean square. The paper reports a small improvement in the resulting lower bound.
classical_zeta_transfer_obstacle: The optimization treats only the dominant term and counts zeros on the line in bulk. It cannot exclude occasional off-line zeros.

title: Généralisation du théorème de Ikehara
venue: Annales Scientifiques de l’École Normale Supérieure 71, 213–242
version: digitized original journal, proceedings or seminar publication
read_scope: Targeted reading of the primary text at Theorems I–II, pp. 213–216.
main_result: For a nondecreasing summatory function with Laplace–Stieltjes transform having the specified one-sided boundary behavior and a controlled singular term, derives an asymptotic A exp(at)P(t). Theorem II relaxes the permitted boundary behavior.
classical_zeta_transfer_obstacle: A Tauberian result derives asymptotics from boundary data. It neither supplies boundary data on the critical line nor excludes internal zeros.

title: Distribution des nombres premiers et fonction ζ(s)
version: digitized original journal, proceedings or seminar publication
read_scope: Targeted reading of the primary text at items 12–14, including the Ikehara application.
main_result: Explains how the nonvanishing of ζ at Re s=1 suffices for the PNT via Ikehara and how stronger zero information produces sharper prime-counting remainders.
classical_zeta_transfer_obstacle: The Tauberian theorem only uses the line Re s=1. It yields no zero exclusion in the open critical strip.

title: Un théorème sur les fonctions arithmétiques multiplicatives et ses applications
venue: Annales Scientifiques de l’École Normale Supérieure 78, 1–29
version: digitized original journal, proceedings or seminar publication
read_scope: Targeted reading of the primary text at §1.1, equations (2)–(3).
main_result: Under its multiplicativity, boundedness and divergence conditions at primes, the paper proves cancellation of the mean over all integers and over squarefree integers, with applications to additive-function distributions.
classical_zeta_transfer_obstacle: Prime-weighted mean cancellation is much weaker than the quantitative cancellation in the Möbius summatory function required for RH.

title: Démonstration élémentaire du théorème des nombres premiers
version: digitized original journal, proceedings or seminar publication
read_scope: Targeted reading of the primary text at statement at items 1–2 and the final elementary argument.
source_locator: statement at items 1–2 and the final elementary argument
main_result: Gives an elementary proof of the prime number theorem, phrased in terms of the asymptotic weighted prime sums and using Selberg's identity.
classical_zeta_transfer_obstacle: The elementary prime number theorem gives an asymptotic of order x without an RH-scale bound for its remainder.

title: Démonstration élémentaire du théorème des nombres premiers

source_locator: pp. 123–127, Selberg identity and deduction of the limit
main_result: A contemporary seminar exposition of the elementary Erdős–Selberg proof, including the weighted identity and passage to the prime number theorem.
classical_zeta_transfer_obstacle: The result determines the main term. It gives no all-zero assertion about the interior of the strip.

title: О нулях дзета-функции Римана
version: digitized original journal, proceedings or seminar publication
read_scope: Targeted reading of the primary text at abstract, introduction equation (1), and the concluding theorem.
source_locator: abstract, introduction equation (1), and the concluding theorem
main_result: Proves ζ(σ+it)≠0 for σ≥1−1/(9.65 log t) with t≥12, using a trigonometric polynomial and a differenced logarithmic derivative.
classical_zeta_transfer_obstacle: An explicit region adjacent to 1 leaves the complementary part of the right half-strip uncontrolled.

title: О функции ζ(s)
version: digitized original journal, proceedings or seminar publication
read_scope: Targeted reading of the primary text at p. 631, equations (1)–(2).
main_result: Announces a bound for ζ(1+it) from a new exponential-sum estimate, with the summed phase given by a multiple of ln x in the stated parameter range.
classical_zeta_transfer_obstacle: The individual value bound is on the right boundary and does not exclude interior zeros.

title: Sur la distribution des nombres premiers
version: original journal PDF with the Note additionnelle on printed p. 182
read_scope: Targeted reading of the primary text at §7 and the Note additionnelle, pp. 181–182.
main_result: Under RH, §7 proves π(x)−Li(x)=O_ε(x^(1/2+ε)). The added note sharpens it to O(x^(1/2) log x).
classical_zeta_transfer_obstacle: The estimate relies on the critical-line hypothesis. Using the remainder to deduce RH would require proving the bound independently.

title: Équirépartition et zéros de la fonction zêta
version: digitized original journal, proceedings or seminar publication
read_scope: Targeted reading of the primary text at pp. 1–3, Landau sums (1)–(2) and Weyl criterion.
source_locator: pp. 1–3, Landau sums (1)–(2) and Weyl criterion
main_result: Removes RH from the equidistribution modulo 1 of logarithmic rescalings of the full ordinates, by combining Landau's weighted zero sums with a bound controlling the real parts, and gives a multidimensional extension for multiplicatively independent scales.
classical_zeta_transfer_obstacle: Uniform distribution modulo 1 of imaginary parts does not distinguish critical-line zeros from off-line zeros.

title: Nombres premiers généralisés et équirépartition modulo 1
version: digitized original journal, proceedings or seminar publication
read_scope: Targeted reading of the primary text at §§1–3, Theorems 1–3.
main_result: Uses a Weyl criterion on generalized integers and generalized primes, with character hypotheses and estimates derived from the generalized prime number theorem.
classical_zeta_transfer_obstacle: The conclusion concerns distribution modulo 1 under generalized prime hypotheses. It places no restriction on every classical zeta zero.

title: Inequalities for zeros of ζ(s)
version: Acta Arithmetica original printed article on two-page archive spreads
read_scope: Targeted reading of the primary text at Theorems 2–3, building on Lemma 1, pp. 255–260.
main_result: Constructs orthonormal families from a decomposition of the Mellin representation and applies Bessel's inequality to restrict possible zeros; Theorem 3 gives explicit zero-free regions.
classical_zeta_transfer_obstacle: The inequalities depend on the constructed family and give the stated restricted regions, without covering the full off-line strip.

title: On the zeros of the Riemann zeta-function and L-series
version: Acta Arithmetica original printed article on two-page archive spreads including neighboring article matter
read_scope: Targeted reading of the primary text at §1, Theorems 1–2, pp. 211–212.
main_result: Starting from one or two zeros with real part greater than 1/2 and ordinate above 100, gives lower bounds for a weighted sum over zeros in specified discs near the 1-line, subject to the stated scale restrictions.
classical_zeta_transfer_obstacle: The conditional neighborhood constraints describe consequences of a hypothetical off-line zero. The bounds do not by themselves contradict its presence.

title: The Zeros of the Riemann Zeta-Function
venue: Proceedings of the Royal Society A 151, 234–255
version: original journal scans on two-page spreads, 22 printed pages in 11 PDF pages
read_scope: Targeted reading of the primary text at §1, pp. 234–235, and closing tables.
main_result: Uses the Riemann–Siegel asymptotic formula with a controlled remainder to locate the first 195 zeros up to ordinate 390 on the critical line.
classical_zeta_transfer_obstacle: The computation has a finite ordinate cutoff. Higher zeros require separate control.

title: Étude sur les propriétés des fonctions entières et en particulier d’une fonction considérée par Riemann
venue: Journal de Mathématiques Pures et Appliquées 9, 171–215
version: digitized original journal, proceedings or seminar publication
read_scope: Targeted reading of the primary text at Part III, §§34–38, pp. 210–215.
main_result: Analyzes the growth and genus of the completed Riemann function, viewed in the squared centered variable, to justify the product structure assumed in Riemann's memoir.
classical_zeta_transfer_obstacle: Entire-function genus gives convergence and structure of a product over zeros. It supplies no theorem forcing the individual factors' zeros to lie on a line.

title: Ω-Theorems for Riemann’s Zeta-Function at Harmonic Combinations of Points
version: original PNAS printed page images assembled from PMC CDN into a PDF
read_scope: Targeted reading of the primary text at main statement and coefficient argument, pp. 1657–1658.
source_locator: main statement and coefficient argument, pp. 1657–1658
main_result: Shows simultaneous large-product lower bounds for zeta values at harmonic ordinates for each fixed integer r≥2. Discusses analogues for fixed real parts between 1/2 and 1 and for reciprocal zeta at 1.
classical_zeta_transfer_obstacle: Large values at selected ordinates are compatible with off-line zeros elsewhere and are logically distinct from zero-free bounds.

title: Ω-Theorems for Quotients of Zeta-Functions at Combinations of Points
version: original PNAS printed page images assembled from PMC CDN into a PDF
read_scope: Targeted reading of the primary text at Theorem A, p. 2528.
main_result: For integers q,r in the stated ranges, proves limsup lower bounds for the absolute value of a quotient of zeta products on the 1-line, with factors indexed by harmonic scales.
classical_zeta_transfer_obstacle: A lower bound along selected sequences on the 1-line cannot exclude zeros further left.

title: Nouvelle démonstration pour la formule de Riemann sur le nombre des nombres premiers inférieurs à une limite donnée et démonstration d’une formule plus générale pour le cas des nombres premiers d’une progression arithmétique
venue: Annales Scientifiques de l’École Normale Supérieure 25, 399–442
version: digitized original journal, proceedings or seminar publication

source_locator: introduction, definition of f(x), and the later progression formula
main_result: Gives a new derivation of Riemann's prime-power counting formula and its extension to primes in a reduced progression, using the appropriate Dirichlet L-series.
classical_zeta_transfer_obstacle: The explicit formula relates primes to a sum over zeros. It continues to require separate estimates or geometric information to locate the zeros.

title: Zur Theorie der Dirichletschen Reihen
venue: Journal für die reine und angewandte Mathematik 134, 95–143
version: GDZ original volume pages extracted without altering printed pp. 95–143 (PDF pages 102–150 of the volume)
read_scope: Targeted reading of the primary text at opening and §§4–5, especially the coefficient-summation integral on pp. 103–104.
source_locator: opening and §§4–5, especially the coefficient-summation integral on pp. 103–104
main_result: Supplies rigorous uniqueness and inversion results for Dirichlet series with increasing real exponents. His integral recovers coefficient sums with a boundary convention for exponents at the cutoff.
classical_zeta_transfer_obstacle: The inversion recovers sums from analytic data in a convergence half-plane. Moving the contour toward the critical line requires additional singularity and error control.

title: Об одной теореме Харди–Литтлвуда в теории дзета-функции Римана
version: Acta Arithmetica original printed article on two-page archive spreads
read_scope: Targeted reading of the primary text at main theorem and (2)–(5), pp. 45–46.
main_result: Under its trigonometric-sum bound with exponent Δ, gives an odd-order critical-line zero in each sufficiently high interval of length T^(1/8+Δ/2) times an arbitrarily slowly increasing factor.
classical_zeta_transfer_obstacle: The interval contains at least one critical-line zero. This is consistent with other zeros in that interval off the critical line.
correction_history: The author returned to this result in the separate 1979 addendum, pp. 403–404, with a Lindelöf specialization and revised remainder estimate.

title: О поведении функций Re{ζ(s)}, Im{ζ(s)} в критической полосе
version: Acta Arithmetica original printed article on two-page archive spreads including neighboring article matter
read_scope: Targeted reading of the primary text at Theorems 1–2 and (1)–(8), p. 25.
main_result: Assuming the stated trigonometric-sum bound, proves that sufficiently high intervals specified in (2) at fixed σ=1/2+δ in the admitted range contain an ordinate where Im ζ vanishes and an ordinate where Re ζ equals 1.
classical_zeta_transfer_obstacle: Zeros of the imaginary part and real-target crossings are different level-set conditions. These results do not distinguish the locations of complex zeros of ζ.

title: Добавление к работе «Об одной теореме Харди–Литтлвуда в теории дзета-функции Римана»
version: Acta Arithmetica original printed addendum on two-page archive spreads including neighboring article matter
read_scope: Read both printed pages. The first applies the Lindelöf exponential-sum formulation to the 1976 theorem and the second changes the truncation in its remainder analysis.
main_result: Under Lindelöf, every sufficiently high critical-line interval of length T^(1/8+ε) contains an odd-order zero. The addendum also refines the earlier remainder estimate by changing the summation cutoff.
classical_zeta_transfer_obstacle: The result is conditional and guarantees a critical-line zero in each interval. It does not locate all zeros there.

title: Sur la fonction ζ(s) de Riemann et sur des fonctions analogues

title: Sur la distribution des entiers ayant certaines propriétés
venue: Annales Scientifiques de l’École Normale Supérieure 73, 15–74
